provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Mechanism: count 4-connected single-colour objects per non-background colour (background = palette[0]); build a bar chart with one bar per colour whose length equals the object count, bars ordered by descending count, filled with palette[0] elsewhere. Canonically bars are rows, right-aligned, largest on top. The factory hand-derives, for each D4 index, the visible bar orientation (rows vs columns), the anchoring edge (start vs end of the bar axis) and whether the largest bar is at index 0 or last: d4=0 rows/right/top; 1 columns/bottom/largest rightmost; 2 rows/left/largest bottom; 3 columns/top/largest leftmost; 4 rows/left/top; 5 columns/top/largest rightmost; 6 rows/right/largest bottom; 7 columns/bottom/largest leftmost. The emitted program builds the output directly in visible coordinates with these constants; no rotation or colour unmapping is performed.
draft_notes.limitations: The generator samples distinct counts per colour, so ties never occur; if they did, the emitted program breaks ties by visible colour value ascending, which under a palette permutation may differ from the canonical (original-colour) tie order. Background is assumed to be palette[0] (always true for this generator). Objects are assumed non-touching across same colour, as guaranteed by the constructor's overlap check with margin 1. Fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule.
draft_notes.host_review: Read constructor and factory. Keep distinct colour counts and2..5square lengths; use bounded rectangle packing with one-cell separation. Solver counts connected objects and draws count-sorted bars with direct D4-specialized order and alignment.
